name: GNAV
description: Gnav is a Scandinavian elimination game from the Cuckoo family. Each round players hold one hidden piece, may stand or try to swap left, and try to avoid finishing with the lowest value.

content.text: Gnav is a Scandinavian elimination game from the Cuckoo family. Each round players hold one hidden piece, may stand or try to swap left, and try to avoid finishing with the lowest value.

Gnav is a traditional round game played in Norway and in some parts of Denmark (for example on the island of Møn) as a family game on Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve. It is closely related to the old Italian game Cuccù, the German Hexenspiel and the Swedish Byteskille; a variant known as Slabberjan is played in Zeeland in the Netherlands.
42 total pieces: two each of Gjok (cuckoo), Dragon, Katt, Hest, Hus, XII-XI-X-IX-VIII-VII-VI-V-IV-III-II-I, 0, Potte, Ugle, and Narr.
Gnav card pack or wooden pawns, plus tokens or matches used as lives and a central pool.
Dealer gives one hidden piece to each player; each player privately checks their own value.

items.text: Double Fool Sit-Out: If both fools are dealt and survive swap round, both holders pay and may skip the next deal.
Slabberjan Related Set: Dutch Slabberjan uses a related 42-piece order and special actions; treat it as a separate ruleset in the same family.
